ghana_factors.material: Portland cement (CEM I) A1-A3, imported-clinker scenario (Egypt-origin EPD proxy)
ghana_factors.geography: Ghana market; clinker predominantly imported, Egypt the leading origin; value from a verified Egyptian CEM I EPD
ghana_factors.module: A1-A3 (full cradle-to-gate, EPD-declared; kiln fuel included)
ghana_factors.proxy_flag: yes (origin EPD used as a Ghana-market scenario; not a Ghana plant EPD)
ghana_factors.formula: Declared GWP-total A1-A3 from Titan Egypt CEM I 52.5 N EPD (A1 1090 + A2 0.9 + A3 34.7)
ghana_factors.inputs_shown: Titan Cement Egypt CEM I 52.5 N (Beni Suef), EPD-IES-0021584:003, EN 15804+A2 (S30). Ghana imports essentially all of its clinker; Egypt was the leading origin in 2022-2024, Tuerkiye before that (S31).
ghana_factors.value_notes: Fills the kiln-fuel gap the screening factor leaves open: because Ghana grinds mostly imported clinker, an Egypt-origin clinker burden (a full A1-A3 EPD, kiln fuel included) is a more defensible Ghana-market OPC headline than the kiln-fuel-excluded screening sum, until a Ghana plant EPD exists. CEM I is a high-clinker (~95%) product; blended and calcined-clay cements are lower.
